I will still do it mostly the way I know, starting from what worked before and only moving a little. On my 6.8 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the steady grain money, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton because cotton can still bring cash if I manage it clean and do not let the worms get ahead of me. I do not like taking risks with fertilizer. If I put a little extra and the crop stands good, I can still harvest. If I save too much on fertilizer and the yield falls, that loss is bigger. I have well water, so I will use that when the ground turns dry instead of waiting too long. For wheat, I will put the stronger fertilizer under before sowing, then add nitrogen when it greens up and again around jointing if the color looks light. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people around me do, give it enough base fertilizer, then topdress when it reaches knee-high to waist-high. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area, use improved seed, not too much water early, then feed it in stages so it sets bolls instead of just making leaves. I will do rotary tillage on the wheat and cotton ground because it is easier for me, and for summer maize after wheat I will keep it simple and go no-tillage if I can, so I do not lose time. I will watch costs, but I will not cut the main things: seed, fertilizer, one or two irrigations at the key time, and enough pesticide sprays to keep insects and disease from taking the crop.
